title: Sample-efficient inductive matrix completion with noise and inexact side-information
summary: Inductive matrix completion (IMC) is a variant of low-rank matrix completion that incorporates row and column side-information. In principle, it can reduce the effective dimension of the recovery problem from the ambient matrix size to the dimension of the side-information features. Existing theory, however, does not fully realize this advantage in the noisy setting: sample-efficient guarantees only apply to noiseless recovery, while noisy guarantees require sample sizes comparable to ordinary matrix completion.
